# Alloy-validation exclusions for the gated test harness
# (Sigil-Logic/clafer#16; consumed by test/Makefile validateAlloyOutput).
#
# Each entry names a generated file under test/positive/ that is
# EXPECTED to be rejected by `java -jar org.alloytools.alloy.dist-6.2.0.jar
# commands`.  Every other generated .als is exit-code-gated; entries
# here are strict expected failures: if Alloy starts accepting one, or
# it stops being generated, the harness fails with a [STALE] error and
# the entry must be removed.
#
# Provenance: all 42 entries are the behavioral (AlloyLtl generator)
# tmp_* family.  They target the Alloy 4.2 stateTrace.als trace
# encoding, which Alloy 6.2 rejects -- primed identifiers became
# temporal-operator syntax in Alloy 6 (see doc/alloy-6.2-migration.md,
# "Corpus audit").  The family is deferred wholesale to
# Sigil-Logic/clafer#11 (behavioral Clafer on Alloy 6 native temporal
# logic); landing #11 must empty this list.  Note the two
# non-temporal behavioral models tmp_DefaultGlobal.als and
# tmp_Global00.als validate clean and are deliberately NOT excluded:
# exclusion is by name, not by tmp_ prefix.
tmp_after01.als
tmp_afteruntil01.als
tmp_before01.als
tmp_betweenand01.als
tmp_clafertransitions01.als
tmp_clafertransitions02.als
tmp_combinedEGX01.als
tmp_combinedEGX02.als
tmp_eventually01.als
tmp_eventually02.als
tmp_eventually03.als
tmp_eventually04.als
tmp_final01.als
tmp_final02.als
tmp_finally01.als
tmp_finally02.als
tmp_Global01.als
tmp_Global02.als

tmp_Global05.als
